module_title: Advanced Analysis - Drainage Patterns, Geomorphology, and Water Disputes
introduction: This advanced level explores the geomorphological reasons behind estuary formation, the concept of consequent drainage, and the socio-political impact of historical river disputes.

core_concepts.title: Consequent Drainage System
core_concepts.description: Himalayan rivers are 'Antecedent' (they existed before the mountains and cut through them). Peninsular rivers are 'Consequent', meaning their course is simply a 'consequence' of the land's natural slope (flowing from the higher Western Ghats to the lower Eastern coast).

core_concepts.title: Why West-Flowing Rivers Don't Form Deltas
core_concepts.description: Narmada and Tapi do not form deltas because: 1. They flow through hard, rocky rift valleys, meaning they erode very little sediment/silt. 2. They have a steep gradient near the sea, so any sediment they do carry is washed deep into the ocean rather than being deposited at the mouth.

core_concepts.title: The Pranhita Confluence
core_concepts.description: The Godavari has a massive catchment area. When the Penganga, Wainganga, and Wardha rivers merge, their combined massive flow is called the 'Pranhita' river, which is the largest tributary of the Godavari.

core_concepts.title: Cauvery Water Dispute
core_concepts.description: One of the oldest and most complex inter-state river water disputes in India. It primarily involves 4 states/UTs: Karnataka (origin state), Tamil Nadu (lower riparian state), Kerala (origin of some tributaries), and Puducherry.

important_entities.name: Jog Falls
important_entities.significance: Also known as Gersoppa Falls or Mahatma Gandhi Falls. It is one of the highest 'plunge' waterfalls in India, created by a small but powerful west-flowing peninsular river.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The massive deltas of the Godavari and Krishna rivers merge near the coastline. Located exactly in the depression between these two advancing deltas is 'Kolleru Lake' (Andhra Pradesh), one of the largest freshwater lakes in India.

The extremely fertile land between the Krishna River and its major tributary, the Tungabhadra, is called the 'Raichur Doab'. Historically, it was the primary cause of continuous wars between the Vijayanagara and Bahmani empires.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Malprabha & Ghatprabha; Panchganga & Dudhganga. Recognizing these 'sister' pairs helps instantly identify them as Krishna's tributaries.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC often asks for the descending order of peninsular river basins by size. The correct order is: Godavari > Krishna > Mahanadi > Cauvery.
In Assertion-Reasoning questions, ensure you link the lack of sediment (due to hard rock beds) and steep slopes directly to the formation of estuaries by the Narmada and Tapi.
